course_name_original: Ciencia e ingeniería de los materiales
prerequisites: No specific prior knowledge is required, but basic notions of chemistry and physics are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and the properties of materials.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction: Materials, Properties and Applications.
BLOCK II. STRUCTURE AND MICROSTRUCTURE OF MATERIALS
Materials Science and Engineering. Types of materials: Classification. Structure-Properties relationship. Applications.
Topic 2. Solid-state structure. Short-range and long-range order. Crystalline structure: Unit cells. Allotropic transformations. Crystalline defects: vacancies, dislocations, and grain boundaries.
Topic 3. Solidification and diffusive processes. Solidification processes in and out of equilibrium. Diffusive processes in the solid state and the laws that govern them.
Topic 4. Binary phase diagrams. Solid solutions and intermediate phases. Equilibrium phase diagrams. Complete and partial miscibility in the solid state. Solid-state transformations.
BLOCK III. PROPERTIES AND IN-SERVICE BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS

Topic 5. Mechanical properties of materials. Stress and strain. Elastic and plastic deformation. Tensile testing. Yield strength, tensile strength, ductility and toughness. Hardness tests. Brittle and ductile fracture. Impact fracture tests. Fatigue failure. Creep failure. Initiation of material wear.
Topic 6. Physical properties of materials. Electrical, thermal, and optical behavior of materials. Electrical and thermal conductivity. Interaction of radiation with matter.
Topic 7. Metallic materials. Ferrous alloys. Non-ferrous alloys. Processing, properties, and applications.
Topic 8. Ceramic materials. Non-crystalline ceramic materials: glasses. Crystalline ceramic materials. Processing, properties, and applications.
Topic 9. Polymeric materials. Polymer structure: polymerization. Thermoplastic polymers. Elastomers: rubber. Thermoset polymers. Processing, properties, and applications.
Topic 10. Composite materials. Constituents of composite materials: matrices and reinforcements. Processing, properties, and applications.
BLOCK V. CORROSION OF METALLIC MATERIALS
Topic 11. Corrosion of metallic materials. Electrochemical fundamentals. Electrode potentials. Corrosion cells. Faraday's Law. Types of corrosion.
assessment_rules: The general evaluation model is continuous assessment. No individual assessment activity can exceed 60% of the overall grade. Non-re-evaluable activities (laboratory work and problem solving) cannot exceed 40% of the overall grade and generally have no minimum mark. Students who do not pass the ordinary call or did not present themselves can take the extraordinary call only for re-evaluable activities (exams) not passed. Exams require a minimum score of 5. Attendance is mandatory for laboratory work and problem-solving activities, and they are not re-evaluable. The advanced call will be evaluated by a single exam covering all course material.
